thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — profiler shows a kernel-selection flip on long sequences that's causing a p95 spike when continuous batching is enabled. p50 flat. Seen on a100x2 instances.

maria: Numbers from yesterday's canary: baseline p95 320ms -> after autotune change 750ms (+2.34x). token/sec throughput roughly the same.

ajay: ugh. which autotune change? commit?

maria: commit: 2f4b9a7 (kernel-selector: prefer fused_gemm_attn_v2 for seq>=512). It works for throughput but launch cost + KV-warmup kills tail when cont-batch groups mixed seqlens.

riley: grabbed a pprof + flamegraph from the failed canary: https://pprof.internal/reports/2189/ — flame shows a big launch stall in gpu_launch and kv_cache_load. small snippet:

```
peak: gpu_launch 320ms
kv_cache_load_miss 210ms
fused_gemm_attn_v2 60ms
matmul_128b_fp16 40ms
```

riley: so fused kernel faster per-token but has a big warmup/handshake penalty when kernel path switches and KV cache cold.

perf-bot: alert: regression_detected commit=2f4b9a7 metric=p95 increase=2.34x test=canary-rtx-a100x2

ajay: ok — reproduction plan? small script that reproduces mixed seqlen arrival and enables cont-batch. we need to measure launch + kv miss as first-class costs per-kernel.

maria: repro: loadgen with distribution {short:80%, long(>512):20%}, contbatch window=12ms, batch size target=32. I can push the script to /infra/perf/repro/2189001234.sh

leo: idea: autotuner objective should be total_expected_latency = expected_kernel_runtime + prob_switch*launch_cost + prob_kv_miss*kv_penalty. if fused has lower kernel_runtime but much higher launch+kv_penalty, the tuner should prefer matmul_128b for mixed traffic.

ajay: propose quick heuristic patch: when contbatch enabled, add hysteresis of 2 consecutive windows before switching kernels for a particular device. plus measure kv_warmup_ms per kernel and require expected win > kv_warmup_ms * alpha (alpha=1.5) to switch.

riley: +1 to hysteresis. Also add a tiny continuous-batch-aware estimator in kernel selector that uses seqlen distribution observed in last N=500 requests rather than single-request seqlen. avoids flip-flop on bursts.

maria: I'll open a ticket with repro, perf traces, and suggested heuristic. we should revert commit 2f4b9a7 on canary and run the patched selector as A/B quickly.

ajay: ticket: https://issues.redwood/s/INF-4721 (created). assigned to @maria and @riley. priority P0 for canary rollback.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline started for rollback branch rollback/INF-4721

maria: quick numbers from a local run with the hysteresis + kv_penalty guard: p95 dropped to 360ms (close to baseline). warmup still visible on first few windows but tail stable.

leo: long-term: we should teach autotuner to sample launch_cost and kv_warmup per kernel per device (periodic microbench) and include that in model. also add config knobs: prefer_lower_launch_cost and contbatch_mode (aggressive|conservative).

riley: will add a lightweight microbench endpoint that runs 3 kernels with synthetic inputs and reports launch and kv metrics. small cron job per GPU node.

maria: next steps: 1) rollback canary 2) merge hysteresis+kv_guard 3) run microbench cron for 24h to populate metrics 4) update tuner objective to include those costs. I'll send a short PR.

ajay: assign me to review the PR, will run throughput/stability job after merge.

riley: tagging infra to keep an eye on KV cache memory while cron runs — we might see transient evictions if we run many microbench tasks.

maria: thx. cc: @perf-bot to keep monitoring p95; we'll annotate the canary and close INF-4721 after stable runs.

perf-bot: monitoring enabled for canary group canary-rtx-a100x2. alert suppression window=2h for rollback.

leo: minor: also consider amortizing launch costs by batching similar seqlen requests into sticky sub-buckets before kernel dispatch. that pairs well with the hysteresis idea.

maria: noted. ok moving to action. short status updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
